description: An ambitious team developing "Sunbula," a smart agricultural robot with tracked mechanisms to scan soil health, moisture, and NPK nutrients using AI and IoT. Connected to a mobile app, it delivers real-time analytics to boost crop productivity and sustainability.
summary:
Sanbola AgTech
Our project, "Sanbola," is an intelligent agricultural robot that bridges the gap between NASA’s satellite data and actual field conditions. Farmers today are struggling with new climatic challenges; they often irrigate and fertilize based on guesswork, lacking the precise knowledge required for their crops—and they generally cannot interpret complex NASA datasets.
We have addressed this with a tracked, ground-based robot equipped with a robotic arm and an NPK sensor that measures soil nutrients (nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium) as well as moisture levels directly in the field. The robot integrates these readings with NASA’s climate data and transmits them to our mobile application, "SANBOL." The app features an AI assistant that provides farmers with precise guidance on when to irrigate and exactly how much fertilizer to apply. Crucially, the system operates entirely offline—ensuring it remains functional for farmers in areas without internet access—and it reduces fuel consumption by 35%, allowing farmers to recover the cost of the device within a single growing season.
details: 1. Function and How It Works Sunbula is a smart agricultural robot designed to bridge the gap between NASA satellite observations and on-ground farming operations. The tracked field rover navigates across crop rows and uses an automated robotic arm equipped with a Soil NPK Sensor to collect real-time ground measurements of essential soil nutrients (Nitrogen, Phosphorus, and Potassium), soil pH, and moisture levels. The system fuses these on-site readings with macro-level satellite climate and soil moisture datasets from NASA. Farmers monitor soil health, control the rover, and interact with SANBOL AI—an integrated smart assistant within our custom SANBOL mobile application—to receive actionable recommendations on irrigation timing and precise fertilization. 2. Benefits * Eliminating Blind Irrigation and Fertilization: Replaces guesswork with data-driven decisions based on real-time soil moisture and nutrient levels, preventing water and resource waste. * Cost Reduction and Higher Crop Quality: Cuts fertilizer expenses by 35% while improving overall crop quality. * Full Offline Operation: Operates completely offline in rural farms lacking internet access by syncing cached NASA satellite datasets and communicating locally through our custom mobile application. * Protection Against Climate Shifts: Provides localized weather tracking and early-warning insights to help protect crops from sudden heatwaves and weather anomalies. 3. Expected Impact * Rapid Return on Investment: Enables farmers to recover the full cost of the robot within a single agricultural season thanks to significant fertilizer savings. * Closing the Space-to-Field Disconnect: Translates complex NASA satellite data into simple, daily farming decisions for small-scale farmers, while also serving large farms, land reclamation companies, and agricultural research centers. * Sustainable Regional Scaling: Promotes resource-efficient farming with a scalable roadmap to support diverse strategic crops across Egypt and arid regions worldwide, alongside future integration with solar-powered automated irrigation grids. 4. Tools, Programming Languages, Hardware, and Software Used * Hardware & Electronics: * ESP32-S3-WROOM-1/1U: A microcontroller module with built-in Wi-Fi and Bluetooth LE used for embedded control, IoT connectivity, and edge AI applications. * Soil NPK Sensor: Measures Nitrogen, Phosphorus, and Potassium levels in the soil for precision fertilization. * RS485 Communication Module: Ensures reliable, long-distance data transfer between the soil sensors and the central controller. * TowerPro MG995 Servo Motors: Controls mechanical actuation for the robotic arm as well as valves and gates for automated irrigation and seeding. * Power Regulation Module: Stabilizes voltage levels to ensure safe and efficient power distribution across the system. * Software & AI: * SANBOL Mobile Application: Custom-built control and monitoring interface featuring a system dashboard, soil analysis, movement controls, and scan history. * SANBOL AI: Smart agriculture chat assistant that analyzes soil readings and provides tailored irrigation and nutrient guidance. * NASA & Open Data Sources: * NASA POWER (power.larc.nasa.gov): Supplies satellite-based temperature, humidity, and solar radiation data. * NASA SMAP (earthdata.nasa.gov): Tracks high-resolution global satellite data for surface and root-zone soil moisture levels. * USDA Ag Data Commons (nal.usda.gov): Provides open-source agricultural research datasets, soil records, and crop production metrics. * Programming & Engineering Tools: * Embedded C++ & Arduino IDE: Used for programming the ESP32-S3 microcontroller, handling RS485 sensor communication, and controlling servo motor actuation. * 3D CAD & Prototyping: Used for designing and fabricating the custom robotic arm and rover chassis. * App & AI Development Stack: Used to build the offline-capable SANBOL interface, local wireless communication protocol, and the SANBOL AI agricultural assistant. 5. Creative & Innovative Aspects * Space-to-Field Data Fusion: Combines macro-level satellite observations from NASA with micro-level physical soil measurements collected directly by a mobile field rover. * Offline-First Architecture: Overcomes rural connectivity barriers by caching satellite datasets beforehand and running local offline control and decision-making directly in the field. * Accessible AI Guidance: Bridges the technical literacy gap by converting complex agronomic and satellite metrics into conversational, easy-to-execute advice via SANBOL AI. 6. Factors Considered by the Team * Rural Connectivity Constraints: Designed the entire control and decision-making workflow to operate 100% offline in remote farmlands without internet access. * Terrain & Field Mobility: Selected a tracked rover chassis to navigate uneven agricultural soil and crop rows reliably. * Economic Feasibility & Business Viability: Balanced the cost structure (55% hardware and sensors, 25% software and cloud development, 20% manufacturing, assembly, and testing) and created flexible revenue streams—including unit sales, periodic leasing, and analytics app subscriptions—to fit diverse customer segments. * Signal Reliability & Electrical Safety: Integrated RS485 communication to prevent data loss over sensor runs and added power regulation to protect electronic components. * Future Scalability: Engineered the platform to support upcoming upgrades, including Computer Vision for autonomous navigation and early crop disease detection, as well as a VEML6075 UV Sensor for real-time UVA/UVB solar stress monitoring.
